title: Global EV sales reach 1.85 million units in July 2026
gist: Global EV sales hit 1.85 million units in July 2026, up 9% year-on-year, with 11.5 million sold year-to-date, but the headline masks extreme regional divergence: subsidy-backed Europe grew 33% y-o-y while North America fell 27% against the pre-tax-credit-removal base. China's domestic market is still down 5% y-o-y yet its penetration rate has pushed above 50% and NEV exports set another monthly record above 500,000 units.

insights.claim: Global EV sales reached 1.85 million units in July 2026, up 9% year-on-year, taking year-to-date 2026 sales to 11.5 million units.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Sets the volume base for downstream lithium, nickel and cathode demand modelling; a 9% global growth rate is far below the battery-capacity build assumptions of the past cycle.
insights.locator: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, specialising in EV and battery

insights.claim: Year-to-date global EV sales growth increased yet again in July 2026 after a turbulent start to the year in both China and North America, meaning the global trend is re-accelerating off a weak H1 base.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The direction of the YTD growth rate, not the monthly print, is the cleaner signal for battery-materials demand; three consecutive improvements would mark the cycle trough.
insights.quote: year-to-date EV sales growth increased yet again in July 2026 following the turbulent start to the year in both China and North America.
insights.locator: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence Senior EV Analyst, George Whitcombe

insights.claim: Benchmark's core framing is that the global EV market is now defined by regional divergence rather than a single global demand curve, with policy in each region setting the local trajectory.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Global EV totals are becoming useless as a trading signal; exposure must be sized region by region against each market's subsidy calendar.
insights.quote: The global EV market continues to be defined by regional divergence.
insights.locator: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence Senior EV Analyst, George Whitcombe

insights.claim: European EV sales grew 33% year-on-year in July 2026 and pushed the region's year-to-date growth to 28%, even as sales fell 17% month-on-month.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Europe is currently the only large region compounding EV volume growth; it is where incremental battery-materials demand is actually being created in 2026.
insights.locator: The European EV market declined 17% m-o-m in July

insights.claim: The 17% month-on-month drop in European EV sales in July is a seasonal artefact of the mid-summer holiday lull in the automotive market, not a demand break.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Fade July and August month-on-month weakness in European auto data; read year-on-year instead to avoid mistaking seasonality for a trend reversal.
insights.quote: which is reflective of the highly seasonal nature of its automotive market as it enters the mid-summer holiday lull it experiences in July and August
insights.locator: The European EV market declined 17% m-o-m in July

insights.claim: The return of EV subsidy schemes across Europe's larger automotive markets over the past 18 months is the identified driver of the region's high growth, making consumer-facing support the decisive variable.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: European EV demand is policy-elastic, so subsidy expiry dates are the calendar to trade; each scheme's end is a forward air pocket in the same way the US tax credit was.
insights.quote: Highlighting the significant impact that consumer facing support has.
insights.locator: Europe's legislative drivers and subsidies continue to support

insights.claim: France's EV sales rose 81% year-on-year in July 2026 and the country hit a record EV penetration rate of 37%.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A 37% record penetration print in a major Western market shows the policy-supported ceiling is far higher than current US levels; a template for what restored incentives can deliver.
insights.quote: it achieved a record penetration rate of 37%
insights.locator: France's EV market saw exceptionally strong EV sales

insights.claim: Germany and the UK grew EV sales 46% and 43% year-on-year respectively in July 2026, confirming the European strength is broad-based across its largest markets rather than a single-country effect.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Breadth across France, Germany and the UK makes the European recovery harder to dismiss as noise and supports European OEM and charging-infrastructure exposure.
insights.locator: Germany and the UK also experienced strong EV sales growth

insights.claim: Spain opened its new 'Auto+' EV subsidy scheme on 4 August 2026 with a maximum base subsidy of EUR4,500 (USD5,190) per new EV passenger car, applications backdated to 1 January 2026, replacing MOVES III which expired at the end of December 2025.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A retroactive subsidy is unusual and converts a policy gap into a rebate windfall for buyers who already purchased; specific, datable catalyst for Spanish EV volumes.
insights.locator: Spain opened its new EV subsidy scheme, 'Auto+'

insights.claim: Spanish EV sales are already up 34% year-to-date on the mere promise of a retroactive subsidy, and Benchmark expects a further wave of growth now that Auto+ applications are actually open.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Spain is the highest-visibility near-term upside surprise candidate in European EV volumes for H2 2026.
insights.quote: the Spanish EV market could experience another wave of growth
insights.locator: Spain's EV market has experienced a strong start

insights.claim: North American EV sales fell 27% year-on-year in July 2026, deepening the regional contraction and leaving the market down 18% year-to-date.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: North America is actively subtracting from global battery-materials demand; US-levered cell and cathode capacity faces utilisation risk into 2027.
insights.locator: The contraction of the North American EV market deepened

insights.claim: The North American contraction is attributed to the weakening of the US legislative and regulatory landscape at the end of 2025, specifically the removal of the federal EV tax credit at the end of September 2025.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Confirms US EV demand was incentive-dependent rather than structurally self-sustaining; any restoration of federal support would be a step-change catalyst, and its absence a persistent drag.
insights.quote: With monthly sales now compared against the extraordinary ramp-up seen before the federal support for EV adoption in the US, by way of a tax credit, was removed at the end of September 2025.
insights.locator: While the North American EV market showed a much more positive picture in Q2

insights.claim: US year-to-date EV sales improved nearly 10 percentage points over Q2 2026, from -33% at the end of Q1 to -24% after Q2, with Q2 sales down only 15% year-on-year.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The Q2 improvement was real but is being reversed by base effects; do not extrapolate the Q2 recovery into H2 without adjusting for the 2025 pull-forward.
insights.locator: The US market had shown a more positive picture in Q2

insights.claim: July marked the return of US year-on-year declines in excess of 30% purely because monthly sales are now being compared against the extraordinary pre-tax-credit-removal ramp-up of Q3 2025.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Expect optically brutal US EV prints through Q3 2026 that are base-effect artefacts; the genuine underlying trend only becomes readable from Q4 2026 onward.
insights.locator: However, July brought the return of negative y-o-y growth rates

insights.claim: Canada has begun allocating permits under an agreement with China that lets Chinese-made EVs enter Canada at a lower tariff rate than the previous 100% surtax, with a first-year quota of 49,000 EVs split across two six-month windows.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A Western market partially reopening to Chinese EVs breaks the assumed one-way ratchet of EV protectionism; watch whether other tariff regimes follow with quota-based carve-outs.
insights.locator: Canada has started allocating permits under its agreement with China

insights.claim: Over half of Canada's 24,500 first-window permits had been allocated by early August, with 2,400 allocated in the first week of August alone, showing rapid uptake ahead of the window closing at the end of August.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Fast quota take-up implies real pent-up Canadian demand for lower-priced Chinese EVs and pressure on incumbent OEM pricing in that market.
insights.quote: over half of the available 24,500 permits have been allocated, with 2,400 permits allocated in the first week of August
insights.locator: The first window closes at the end of August

insights.claim: Chinese EV sales were down just 5% year-on-year in July 2026, improving the market's year-to-date growth rate to -12% and confirming a recovery from a slow start to the year.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The world's largest EV market is still contracting in absolute terms; the improving second derivative is the bullish part, not the level.
insights.quote: China resumed showing signs of recovery after its slow start to the year, with EV sales down just 5% year-on-year in July.
insights.locator: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence Senior EV Analyst, George Whitcombe

insights.claim: Further tax changes and potential revisions to China's vehicle trade-in scheme in 2027 are partly driving the current recovery in Chinese EV demand.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Pull-forward risk: if buyers are pre-empting 2027 policy changes, part of the 2026 recovery is borrowed demand that reverses later.
insights.locator: Further tax changes and potential revisions

insights.claim: Chinese NEV exports set another monthly record in July 2026 with more than 500,000 units shipped overseas, as Chinese automakers turn abroad for growth against a subdued domestic market.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Record exports into a weak home market mean intensifying price competition in Europe, Latin America and other open markets; margin risk for Western OEMs and a driver of further tariff action.
insights.quote: more than 500,000 units were shipped overseas
insights.locator: Chinese NEV exports achieved another monthly record in July

insights.claim: China's EV penetration rate has risen above 50% so far in 2026, with multiple months above 60%, versus 48% in the first seven months of 2025 - and it is rising because the total vehicle market is declining faster than EV sales.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A rising penetration rate here is a symptom of ICE collapse, not EV strength; do not read Chinese penetration headlines as a battery-demand upgrade.
insights.quote: its penetration rate has continued to increase with the total vehicle market experiencing a sharper decline in sales
insights.locator: Despite the decline in EV sales in China so far this year
